texts: An athlete with a bicuspid valve has symptomatic severe aortic regurgitation with a dilated left ventricle, significant mitral regurgitation and an ascending aorta of 3.7 cm.
The best operation is aortic valve replacement with mitral valve repair.
His aortic regurgitation is severe, with a vena contracta over 0.6 cm and an orifice of 0.3 cm², and he has symptoms, so the valve must be replaced.
The mitral regurgitation, with flow reversal in the pulmonary veins, is significant and is repaired at the same operation rather than left to worsen.
With a bicuspid valve, the ascending aorta is replaced during another cardiac operation once it reaches 4.5 cm; at 3.7 cm it is left alone.
In the picture, Franky fits new dentures and Usopp sews a brass ring on the mitre, while the white tube for the neck is set aside.
Memory hook: two leaking doors and one healthy neck: fix both doors.
